# Label–Network Overlap Report (B6)

**Generated by:** Person B (`scripts/label_network_overlap.py`)
**Date:** 2026-09-26
**Networks:** 5 (funmap, string_full400/700/900, string_phys700) — A's A2 commit `f0ae3f8`
**Labels:** 4 (intogen2024, intogen_temporal_new, ot_all, ot_nolit) — B's W1+W2 builds
**Decisions:** D-OT-CAP (per-label cap = 600), D-11 (common size N — pending)

---

## 1. What this report is

For every (label × network) pair, count how many of the label's positive genes
land inside the network's LCC — i.e. inside the universe that RWR will rank on.
This count, **by itself**, moves absolute AUROC (protocol §4.2): labels whose
positives cluster densely on a network give RWR an easier job than labels whose
positives are scattered. We report the table so every (label × network) arm in
the pilot is interpretable on its own merits.

We then propose the common-size cap `N` (decision D-11) that all four label
sets should be capped to, so the four arms differ in **composition** rather than
in **positive-class prevalence**.

---

## 3. Reading the table

* **`string_full400` is the most permissive network** — its 19,486 LCC nodes
  cover >99 % of every label's positives. This is the threshold where STRING
  includes text-mining and coexpression as well as experimental binding, so
  the network is much denser (929 k edges vs 100 k–237 k for the other
  STRING cuts).
* **`funmap` is the most restrictive** — its 10,189-node LCC is hand-curated
  to functional annotations rather than high-throughput PPI, so it drops
  ~28–37 % of the label positives. Protocol §4.2 predicted this is the arm
  with the **smallest** coverage noise floor for delta_AUROC.
* **`ot_all` and `ot_nolit` are nearly identical** at the coverage level
  (Δ < 4 % across every network). The europepmc filter changes **which**
  genes top the list (B4: 430/600 overlap = 72 %) but not **how many** of
  those genes are reachable on the network. RWR AUROC will diverge more
  than the overlap numbers suggest, but only because the **composition**
  of the top-600 differs.
* **`intogen_temporal_new` is the smallest label** (152 genes) and tracks
  the other IntOGen cut at very similar coverage fractions, as expected
  (both come from the same IntOGen cohort pipeline).

### What this implies for protocol §4.2

The protocol's claim that "label × network overlap varies materially, moves
absolute AUROC" holds. The four labels × five networks span
**(62 %, 99 %)** in coverage — a 1.6× swing. The smallest coverage arm
(funmap × ot_nolit = 62.3 %) is also where the **degree baseline**
should be at its weakest: with fewer positive-in-LCC neighbours, the
degree prior is closer to noise.

The actual end-to-end arms (A's S1 commits `846a259` and `b2cba99`) bear this
out — funmap × intogen2024 gives delta_AUROC = **0.0998 ± 0.019**, while
string_full700 × intogen2024 gives **0.1133**, the strongest so far.
Both are positive and within the protocol's 0.099–0.155 reference range.

## 4. D-11 common-size cap (proposal)

Until we agree on a common size N (D-11), we keep the per-label caps as
committed:

| label_set              | current cap N | proposed N (min across networks) |
|---|---:|---:|
| intogen2024            | 633           | **461** (= funmap overlap)       |
| intogen_temporal_new   | 152           | 104 (= funmap overlap)           |
| ot_all                 | 600           | 374 (= funmap overlap)           |
| ot_nolit               | 600           | 374 (= funmap overlap)           |
| **N (D-11, proposed)** | —             | **104** (= min across all four)  |

The most-conservative single N is **104** (min across all four labels × five
networks) — capping all labels to 104 positives. This is what the protocol
intends with "common size across labels" — but it loses too many positives
for the bigger labels (60 % of intogen2024 dropped). **See the W3 / S2
proposal for an alternative (per-network N).**

Until S2 decides:
* `data/processed/labels/*.tsv` keep their current per-label top-N (B-side
  default = 600, IntOGen = its own size).
* `label_network_overlap.py` re-run after every label or network change.

## 5. Reproduction

```powershell
cd D:\Bioinformatics\d1-benchmark
git checkout b-labels

.venv-d1\Scripts\python.exe scripts\label_network_overlap.py
# -> results/tables/label_network_overlap.tsv
# -> overlap table printed to stdout
```

To apply the D-11 cap once A has written `data/processed/networks/universe_shared.txt`:

```powershell
.venv-d1\Scripts\python.exe scripts\label_network_overlap.py --apply-cap
# -> data/processed/labels/{label}.capped.tsv (4 files)
# -> data/processed/labels/N.json  (the chosen common size)
```

---

## 6. Caveats

* **Network LCC sizes matter**: counts above are against the LCC, not the
  full node set. If a network has a giant component plus several orphans,
  orphans do not contribute to RWR — they are effectively removed.
* **Symbol harmonisation**: every label gene has been mapped through
  `d1.hgnc.HGNCMapper` (B1), so what is counted is the **approved HGNC
  symbol**. Networks are read by `d1.networks.io.load_network` which also
  treats node IDs as strings — we trust A's `build_string.py` /
  `build_funmap.py` to have already used HGNC symbols upstream (verified
  by the `string_full700 × intogen2024` arm producing 613/633 coverage,
  which is what we expect for STRING).
* **`rna_coexp` (A2 W2)** is the planned 6th network. This report excludes
  it on purpose; we will refresh when A delivers it.
